Commentary.Commentary: Earlier in the innings, Amla scored a half-century with some support from Bavuma and de Kock. Whereas Wagner and Boult picked up 3-fers for the Kiwis. Now Steyn and Co. will have to come to the party to get their side on the front foot. They would be happy with the movement the Kiwi bowlers got this morning and would look to implement the same. Stay tuned as the second innings get underway soon.

What a short spell of cricket! New Zealand came firing in this morning with some fiery quick bowling with the ball swinging in all directions. Southee sent back Steyn without a score on the board for Day 2. After that, it was a lone wicket to be taken and with ball doing so much, it would have been regulation for the Kiwi bowlers. But to everyone's wonder, the last wicket added 27 runs giving the South African bowlers something to work with.

The ball doesn't swing back like it was doing earlier and Piedt gets a faint outside edge  on it. The ball goes back to the keeper who steps to his right and catches it. A muted celebration from NZ and a slightly disappointed Piedt walks back. That was a decent partnership to end the innings. SOUTH AFRICA ARE ALL OUT FOR 263!

EDGED BUT SAFE! Southee making things happen! Around off, swinging away, Piedt hangs his bat in the air to defend but gets an outside edge just short of the second slip fielder.

FOUR! UNLUCKY SOUTHEE! Pitched around middle and leg, swings away after pitching, Piedt looks to defend it from within the crease with a straight bat but gets an outside edge safely through the gap between slips and gully for a boundary. Southee has got this new ball moving bang on!
That's sharp from Southee! Full inswinging delivery on middle and leg, Rabada does well to clip it through mid-wicket for a single.

His defence has a big gap between the bat and the pads and the ball swings in through it removing the bails. That was a clean wicket, removing the bails and going over the keeper. Southee is either impressed or surprised and simply raises his eyebrows.

The players and umpires are out in the middle. The lights are on, the sky is overcast and the second new ball is two overs away. KAGISO RABADA and DALE STEYN to continue batting while DOUG BRACEWELL will resume his over.
Update 1415 IST - We have a respite from the showers and the covers are being taken off. The umpires have inspected the grounds and we should see a 1420 IST start of play.

Update 1350 IST - More covers are being brought on. This indicates that play will be further delayed. Let's hope that the rain gods show us some mercy and stay away giving us some cricketing action on Day 2. Stay tuned for further updates.

Update 1330 IST - The drizzle is back and so are the covers. THE START OF THE MATCH IS SURE TO BE DELAYED as the ground is not be fit for play at the moment. Another concern is the bad lighting conditions, the reason why we saw a premature end to yesterday's play. We will keep you posted with further updates.

The Proteas had their moments throughout the day, with Hashim Amla, Temba Bavuma and Quinton de Kock punishing the bowlers around the park. They will look to add a few more runs in the morning session to set a respectable lead over the visitors. There was a light drizzle over Durban earlier in the morning and we might see some intermittent showers throughout the day. The primary concern is the damp outfield which was already quite bumpy yesterday. Stay tuned for another day of exciting cricket between these two well-balanced sides.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between South Africa and New Zealand. The Kiwis claimed the previous day with a comprehensive bowling performance. Trent Boult was the star of the show, placing the hosts on the back foot early on and Neil Wagner and Mitchell Santner kept them there. With 8 wickets in the bag, it will not be soon before they have a bat as well.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

The first session was an evenly matched affair while New Zealand struck back in the second. The final session of the day was leaning in South Africa's favour but the Kiwis prevailed to end the day. The visitors have thoroughly impressed with their bowling, especially Trent Boult with Wagner and Santner delivering the goods too. Join us tomorrow for all the action on Day 2 at 1330 IST. Until then... goodbye and take care!

de Kock's arrival was an adrenaline boost to the home side as they got going in lightning fashion. de Kock's furious batting rubbed off on Bavuma who also opened up. However, de Kock got too carried away and a Bracewell diving catch ousted him. The wickets fell hot and fast after him, with Santner taking two in an over and Wagner completing his 3-fer.

The umpires have called off the day's play due to the bad light conditions so THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1. The game has so far swung back and forth but ultimately the tourists have had the last laugh. Bavuma and du Plessis set up a patient start to the final session, scoring carefully and not taking too many chances. Their 54-run stand was rudely interrupted by a stunning catch by skipper Williamson and de Kock walked onto the pitch.
The players walk off the field as the dim lighting conditions aren't conducive to a proper day's play.

Welcome back to the final session of the day. The players and umpires are back on the ground. Light could be an issue toward the end of this session. FAF DU PLESSIS and TEMBA BAVUMA are set to continue the batting while TRENT BOULT will resume the bowling proceedings.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

South Africa have Faf du Plessis and Temba Bavuma out in the center right now. They've taken a rather cautious approach and have slowly built their partnership, which is now of 40 runs. With the way they're playing right now, seems this pair intends to see the day off without further damage, as any more wickets could see them in some real trouble. Join us in a short while for the final session of the day. Should be an intriguing one, if anything.

27 overs, 52 runs and 2 wickets - New Zealand have slowly crawled their way back into this session. They've restricted the flow of runs quite nicely and scalped a couple of wickets as well. Once again, it was Neil Wagner who got things going for the Kiwis. Not too long after the break, he took the wicket of JP Duminy and broke the partnership. And it wasn't long before Hashim Amla, who was looking in fine, fine form, departed after completing his half century. Trent Boult was the man once more who delivered.

Things changed with the arrival of the accomplished Hashim Amla. South Africa then introduced southpaw JP Duminy to maintain the right-left combination. Their tactic paid off, with the experienced duo taking back control. A furious 53-run stand in 60 balls ensued as the batsmen sent the fielders scattering to the deep. Both sides have now fired their salvos and are settling in. Join us at 1640 IST as we follow the developments in this match.

An evenly divided session between the two side. New Zealand kept the pressure up in the first half of the session with the batsmen on their toes and the runs coming few and far between. Southee, Boult and Bracewell gradually lured the batsmen out and picked up the scalp of Cook and Elgar. Thus far, it seemed like New Zealand's session all the way.

New Zealand has made one team change since their series in Zimbabwe as Doug Bracewell replaces Ish Sodhi.
New Zealand (Playing XI)- Martin Guptill, Tom Latham, Kane Williamson(c), Ross Taylor, Henry Nicholls, BJ Watling(wk), Mitchell Santner, Doug Bracewell, Tim Southee, Neil Wagner, Trent Boult.
South Africa (Playing XI)- Stephen Cook, Dean Elgar, Hashim Amla, Faf du Plessis(c), Jean-Paul Duminy, Temba Bavuma, Quinton de Kock(wk), Vernon Philander, Dale Steyn, Kagiso Rabada and Dane Piedt.
TOSS - South Africa wins the toss and elects to bat first against New Zealand.
The toss has been delayed by half an hour due to a wet outfield, pushing the start of the match to 1400 IST. Conditions are humid with thick cloud cover and there might be chances of rain later on.

New Zealand, on the other hand, have a young, fresh side that is showing great cohesion. Their captain, Kane Williamson, has proven himself against Zimbabwe and is ready to head down south and attempt the same with the Proteas. His side have displayed great depth in their batting and bowling and, breaking away from history, seem like the stronger side this time. Shaping up to be a competition between the old and new, let's see whether experience or youthful vigour triumphs!

Hello and a warm welcome to the first Test of the two-match series between South Africa and New Zealand. The hosts are currently at seventh spot in the ICC Test rankings, two ranks below New Zealand, which is a change that they will not be happy to see. Their woes do not end there, with a trifecta of problems plaguing their side. The loss of AB de Villiers and Morne Morkel to injury, the unfamiliar Test matches in August and the revamped selection targets.
